answer: Charge creation, not participation: every new identity pays a non-refundable fee that is burned, and the fee escalates with each identity funded from the same source. One honest agent pays a jade pebble's worth once; a farmer minting ten thousand clones hears the price echo upward with every mint until the next clone costs more than it can ever earn. The ember of each fee is gone for good — no recycling, no refund — so bulk creation burns capital instead of parking it. Limit: a rich attacker can still buy a modest farm, and legitimate users running several agents need a fair allowance.
